commit: ce0445a on branch worktree-wf_35876db9-f44-2 (Session Library: persistent drift index, folder scan, search/filters, PB badges). Not pushed, no AI attribution.
done:
The Sessions screen is now a real library instead of the import-only screen.
- "Open now" shows this run's sessions as cards, with the current one highlighted and a close action. Closing now actually releases the DuckDB connection.
- "Library" lists every indexed session, newest recording first. It has word-wise, accent-folded search over track, layout, car, class and driver. It also has Type, Class and Track filter chips with counts. Track chips fold to 8 plus a "+N more" toggle, and a selected chip is never folded.
- Personal-best badges are keyed on track, layout and car class. A best is computed over the whole library, so filtering never moves the badge. The tooltip says "fastest of N sessions".
- Rows reopen from the index, with a stat check first. Missing, changed-on-disk and uploaded rows say so in words. "Remove from library" offers Undo and never touches the file. A missing row is still tappable, so a restored file works without a rescan.
- "Add folder" (file_picker, LMU default folder suggested on Windows) scans a folder sequentially with progress and a Stop button. It skips unchanged files by size and mtime, names every file it could not read, and remembers folders. Refresh rescans and re-checks every row's file status.
- The index is a drift SQLite file on desktop and in memory on web. It is written at import time and refreshed by scans. The bug is fixed: tapping an open-session card now makes it current before navigating.
- Also in: animated row enter/exit, reduced-motion handling, hover and keyboard focus, Cmd/Ctrl-F to focus search, Esc to clear it, and stated empty and error states.
- A previous agent's half-finished work was completed. The 6 analyzer issues are fixed, and a real bug was found and fixed: "Clear filters" left the search box showing old text.

data_findings:
- Real scan of the three samples on macOS (compiled app): 257 ms cold for 3 files including drift writes. Per-file read is 29 ms (Interlagos, 8.8 MB), 32 ms (Spa, 13.6 MB) and 31 ms (Sebring Race, 25.4 MB), so read time does not scale with file size. A rescan with nothing changed took 3 ms (stat only, no file opened).
- Index values read by the real Dart path agree with the independently generated fixture: Interlagos GT3 Practice 3 closed / 2 timed, best 97.30029 s (lap 3), 1 clock gap. Spa Hyper Qualify 4 closed / 1 timed, best 122.73663 s (lap 3), 1 gap. Sebring Race 19 closed / 16 timed, best 63.94092 s (lap 11), 0 gaps. Checked-in fixture laps 0-3: 4 closed / 3 timed, best 64.02963 s (lap 4), read independently with Python duckdb from Lap Time at the Lap boundaries.
- Two real sessions at the same layout and class rank correctly: Sebring Race 1:03.941 beats the fixture's 1:04.030, so the badge sits on the Race and the tooltip says "fastest of 2 sessions".
- The fixture's mtime is 1790726677.7102625 s. Unix-seconds storage, drift's default, would truncate the .710 and make every rescan see a changed file. Hence store_date_time_values_as_text plus an integer modifiedMs column. Verified by the integration test (row.modifiedMs equals the stat value to the millisecond) and by an untouched rescan reporting 3 of 3 unchanged.
- Scanning holds no connection: after a scan, container.exists(telemetrySessionProvider(source)) is false for every file. A non-DuckDB file named broken.duckdb is reported by name ("Could not open telemetry file...") and retried on the next scan.
- Closing a session releases its connection. A DuckDB handle captured before close throws TelemetryQueryException afterward. The provider element still exists after ref.invalidate, so `container.exists` is the wrong check for this. Reopening reads the file afresh and gives a new handle.
- Flutter findings: a widget test over the default drift store never settles (its isolate is outside the fake clock). A zero-duration AnimatedSize asserts in its own performLayout. SliverAnimatedList builds lazily, so finders miss rows below a 900 px viewport once Open now cards sit above them.
- macOS sandbox is off in both entitlement files, so stored paths reopen after a restart. A sandboxed build would need security-scoped bookmarks.
- Golden size note: the long Spa label "Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps — Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps Endurance" is ellipsized at 1000 px. At 1280 px it fits.
spec_notes:
§8.1 (draft): Built in v0.11: the Session Library is a two-list screen. "Open now" shows this run's sessions with the current one lit and a close action. Closing now releases the DuckDB connection, because the session provider is kept alive and dropping it from the list alone left the file open until quit. "Library" is the persistent index, newest recording first. It is searched word-wise and accent-folded across track, layout, car, class and driver, and filtered by session type, car class and track+layout chips that carry counts. Chips exist only for values present, and a group of more than eight folds to eight plus a "+N more" toggle, never hiding a selected chip. The personal-best badge is keyed on (TrackName, TrackLayout, CarClass) and computed over the whole library regardless of filters. Layout is load-bearing for the reason given above. Class is the same mistake one dimension over, since a Hypercar run would otherwise take the badge from every GT3 session. The car is deliberately not in the key. None of the three samples shares a layout across classes, so the class split is structural rather than measured. Rows reopen from the index after a stat check. Missing, changed-on-disk and uploaded rows say so in words. "Remove from library" forgets the row with an Undo and never touches the file. "Add folder" and Refresh scan a folder sequentially, opening each file read-only just long enough to read metadata, laps and the clock scan and then closing it (not through telemetrySessionProvider). The scan skips files whose size and mtime match, names every file it could not read, and can be stopped. There is no watcher: a watcher would index a recording LMU is still writing. The fix for the Phase 1 card that navigated without selecting is also in: tapping an open card makes it current first.

§9.6 (draft): The index is a drift SQLite file in the app-support directory, separate from the recordings. There is one row per path with every §8.1 metadata fact, completed/timed lap counts, best lap and which lap, clock-gap count, size, mtime, importedAt and lastOpenedAt, plus a folders table. Dates are stored as ISO text and mtime as an integer, so change detection is exact to the millisecond. SessionIndexStore is the seam. Web uses an in-memory implementation by decision, because an upload has no path to reopen from and a persisted row could only say "upload this again". Search, filtering, ranking and PB logic live above the store in plain Dart, so the two stores cannot disagree.

§14 (draft): Findings from building the Library. (1) The real scan costs about 30 ms per file whatever its size: 29, 32 and 31 ms for 8.8, 13.6 and 25.4 MB. The three samples index in 257 ms cold and rescan in 3 ms, because unchanged files are skipped on a stat alone. (2) mtime must be stored as an integer: the fixture's 1790726677.7102625 s would be truncated by Unix-seconds storage and every rescan would see a change. (3) Closing a session needs an explicit invalidate of telemetrySessionProvider, and a captured handle throws afterward, whereas `container.exists` stays true, so it is not evidence of release. (4) A widget test over the default drift store never settles, since its isolate is outside the fake clock. The default store is in-memory under FLUTTER_TEST, and real SQL is covered by NativeDatabase.memory() in the unit suite and a temp SQLite file in the compiled integration test. (5) A zero-duration AnimatedSize asserts in its own layout, so reduced motion drops the animation rather than zeroing it. (6) macOS sandbox is off, so stored paths reopen across launches. A sandboxed build would need security-scoped bookmarks. (7) Not measured: the class half of the PB key, since the samples share no layout across classes.
